key_insight: GeRo converts Vision–Language–Action models into generative planners by using autoregressive, language-grounded rollouts that jointly predict future traffic scenes and driving actions, enabling multi-step scenario generation and planning.
problem_solved: Overcomes reliance on sparse trajectory imitation and the under-utilization of VLA models' generative potential, which limits robust planning, interpretability, and scalable scenario/data generation for end-to-end autonomous driving.
method: Plug-and-play GeRo wrapper for VLA models that augments them with generation capabilities while preserving existing planning interfaces.
Autoregressive rollout strategy: iteratively generate language-grounded future scene descriptions and corresponding actions to produce multi-step scenario rollouts.
Use generated rollouts as interpretable predictions and synthetic scenarios for training, evaluation, and robust planning.
impact: Provides richer supervision and interpretable planning signals, enabling scalable synthetic scenario generation and improved robustness/data-efficiency for researchers and engineers building end-to-end driving systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing VLA model + GeRo wrapper and the autoregressive loop (scene -> language description -> action -> next scene).
Before vs after comparison chart (imitation-only vs GeRo) illustrating gains in scenario coverage, interpretability, or robustness.
Storyboard/example rollout: sequence of traffic frames with generated language annotations and planned actions over time.
Icons/visual cues for 'plug-and-play', language balloons, steering/action arrows, and a rollout timeline.
paper_title: Generative Scenario Rollouts for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
paper_authors: Rajeev Yasarla, Deepti Hegde, Shizhong Han, Hsin-Pai Cheng, Yunxiao Shi
